title: Finite-ring bounded lisse complexes and finite derived isomorphism sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $B$ a finite commutative ring. On the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] use $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and constant coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. If $K$ is bounded and every cohomology sheaf is locally constant with finite $B$-module stalks, there is an etale covering on which $K$ is isomorphic to the constant sheaf complex associated to a bounded complex of finite $B$-modules. For two such complexes $K,L$, the sheafification on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ of $V\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{D(V_{\mathrm{et}},B)}(K|_V,L|_V)$ is finite locally constant; locally on constant models $E,G$ its fibre is $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(E,G)$. The analogous sheaf of isomorphisms is finite locally constant, possibly empty. On a connected $X$, for any geometric point $\bar x$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], $K$ is etale locally isomorphic to the constant complex $K_{\bar x}$. No finite Tor dimension is assumed.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant. Agent extension of Tag 09BE, lemma-locally-constant-map, from perfect source to bounded finite source and bounded target by a finite free approximation; finite derived Hom and connected constancy are agent arguments

proof.text: Choose $a\leq b$ outside which the cohomology of $K$ vanishes. A finite ring $B$ is Noetherian: every ideal is finite and is generated by all its elements. Trivialize each cohomology sheaf locally. On a nonempty trivializing member its constant value identifies with a geometric stalk, hence is finite and therefore finitely generated as a $B$-module. The general site bounded-constant-model theorem applies to the small etale site (with its chosen size convention) and its final object $X$. It yields local constant models concentrated in $[a,b]$ with finitely generated terms. Each such term is finite, being a quotient of $B^r$ for some finite $r$. This proves the first clause without a Tor hypothesis. For $K=0$ the zero complex is a model, and for the empty scheme the empty covering suffices.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, strengthened constant-model assertion in the induction

proof.text: Apply step 1 separately to $K$ and $L$. Refine by $U_i\times_X W_j$: these are etale over $X$ and jointly surjective because each of the two families is. On each member write the restrictions as $\underline E$ and $\underline G$, with $E,G$ bounded finite-module complexes. For every bounded finite-free complex $F$ and chain map $F\to E$, each cone term $F^{i+1}\oplus E^i$ is a finite set, so its cohomology is finite (a quotient of a subgroup). The finite-cone free-model theorem applies over $B$ and produces a quasi-isomorphism $P\to E$ with finite-free terms and $P^i=0$ above an upper bound $e$ for $E$. This invokes its statement, not its construction, and does not assert that $E$ is perfect.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, and agent finite-module Hom argument

proof.text: With $P\to E$ as above, choose $g$ with $G^i=0$ for $i<g$ and $m\leq\min(e,g-2)$. Let $F=\sigma_{\geq m}P$: it has the terms $P^i$ for $m\leq i\leq e$, and zero elsewhere. It is bounded finite free. The inclusion into $P$ is an isomorphism on cohomology for $i>m$ and surjective for $i=m$, directly from cycles modulo boundaries. Compose with $P\to E$ and take its cone $C$. The long exact sequence gives $H^i(C)=0$ for $i\geq m$. Orthogonality gives $\operatorname{Hom}(C,G)=\operatorname{Hom}(C[-1],G)=0$, because $C\in D^{\leq m-1}$ and $C[-1]\in D^{\leq m}$ while $G\in D^{\geq g}$. Exactness of Hom out of the cone triangle, and its rotations, now identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(E,G)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(F,G)$ by precomposition.

source.place: Tag 09BE, lemma-locally-constant-map: agent extension using a bounded finite-free approximation; cone calculation as in Tag 064U

proof.text: All terms of $F,E,C$ are finite. Apply exactness of constant finite-module sequences to the cycles, boundaries and cohomology sequences of $C$. It gives $H^i(\underline C)=\underline{H^i(C)}$. Termwise constant sheaves commute with the finite direct sums, differentials and signs in the cone. Thus the constant cone lies in $D^{\leq m-1}$ on every localized etale site, while $\underline G$ lies in $D^{\geq g}$. The same orthogonality and Hom-out-of-triangle exactness as in step 3 give $\operatorname{Hom}(\underline E,\underline G)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(\underline F,\underline G)$ on every etale object. These bijections commute with restriction: they are all precomposition by the restriction of the single fixed map $\underline F\to\underline E$. Here constant complexes and restrictions are those in the constant-complex and derived-map-presheaf definitions.

source.place: Tag 09BE, lemma-locally-constant-map, finite-source extension; exact constant sequences from etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03RX

proof.text: Let $H=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(F,G)$. Since each finite free $B$-module is projective (lift the images of its basis along any surjection), the bounded-projective derived-map-representative theorem identifies $H$ with chain maps $F\to G$ modulo homotopy. Taking constant complexes gives a natural map from the constant presheaf $H$ to the derived Hom presheaf of $\underline F,\underline G$. It is locally surjective: local-actual (1) represents every derived morphism by a chain map after a cover. Apply the constant-sheaf morphism lemma to its finitely many components. On a common refinement every component is induced by a $B$-linear map $F^i\to G^i$. On a nonempty member, taking any geometric stalk turns the chain equations into the same equations for these module maps, by the constant-stalk identification. They therefore form a chain map $F\to G$, and its class in $H$ induces the original local derived morphism. Empty members contribute no sections to check.

source.place: Tag 08FR, lemma-local-actual (1); Tag 09BE, lemma-locally-constant-map, and sites-modules.tex Tag 093S

proof.text: For local injectivity, take two algebraic chain maps whose images agree in actual derived Hom on an etale object. Their difference becomes null-homotopic after a cover by local-actual (2). There are finitely many homotopy components $h^i:\underline F^i\to\underline G^{i-1}$. The constant-sheaf morphism lemma makes them module maps on a common refinement. A geometric stalk on any nonempty member turns $\alpha^i=d_G^{i-1}h^i+h^{i+1}d_F^i$ into an algebraic homotopy, so the two classes in $H$ agree. If their images agree only in sheafified Hom, the site sheafification-sections lemma first makes the equality actual after a cover. This proves local injectivity in that case as well. Together with step 5 and that lemma, the induced map of sheafifications is bijective: locally represent a target section, lift it by step 5, and glue the lifts; on overlaps local injectivity makes their images agree in the source sheaf. Uniqueness follows in the same way. The set $H$ is finite since there are finitely many degreewise maps $F^i\to G^i$ and only finitely many nonzero degrees. Steps 3 and 4 identify this constant Hom sheaf with the constant finite set $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(E,G)$. Applying this on the common cover of step 2 proves the asserted Hom clause for $K,L$.

source.place: Tag 08FR, lemma-local-actual (2); sites.tex Tags 00WB/00WK, theorem-plus and lemma-sections-sheafification; finite Hom calculation

proof.text: Under the Hom-sheaf identification, the sheafification of the isomorphism presheaf is the constant subset $\operatorname{Isom}_{D(B)}(E,G)$. Indeed an algebraic isomorphism and its inverse give inverse constant derived maps. Conversely, if a constant algebraic map represents an actual derived isomorphism on a nonempty etale object, an exact geometric stalk functor takes its inverse to an inverse in $D(B)$, so the map was an algebraic isomorphism. A germ coming from a sheafified isomorphism can be represented by an actual isomorphism after a cover by the site sheafification-sections lemma. Equalities with the local constant Hom representative can be made actual after a further cover, so the preceding test applies to germs as well. On overlaps the algebraic isomorphism representatives agree after refinement by the local injectivity proved for Hom; the same site-sections lemma then glues them to the constant isomorphism sheaf, with uniqueness. Hence the isomorphism sheaf is finite locally constant; its value is the empty set when the two model objects are not isomorphic. Exactness and the constant-stalk theorem are used on underlying abelian groups, and their naturality with multiplication by every $b\in B$ makes the same maps $B$-linear.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, and agent finite-module Hom argument

proof.text: Suppose $X$ is connected and $\bar x$ is a geometric point, and set $E_0=K_{\bar x}$. For each local model $\underline E_j$ on a nonempty cover member $U_j$, exact stalks and the constant-stalk identification give $K_{\bar y}\simeq E_j$ for every geometric point of $U_j$. Define $O\subseteq X$ as the union of the images of those members whose model is isomorphic in $D(B)$ to $E_0$. These images are open because etale morphisms are open. The complement is the union of the images of the other members: an overlap would give a geometric point and identify their two fibres, contradicting the different isomorphism classes. Thus $O$ is both open and closed and contains $x$. Connectedness forces $O=X$. Every nonempty member therefore has $E_j\simeq E_0$, and composing this algebraic isomorphism with its local-model isomorphism gives an etale covering trivializing $K$ as $\underline{K_{\bar x}}$. This proves the connected clause globally, not only near $\bar x$. No step used a finite Tor bound. The empty scheme has no geometric point, so this clause is vacuous. Stalk identifications used here respect the $B$-action, since they are natural for multiplication by each $b\in B$.
